You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def comps_of(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; res=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j] and not seen[i][j]:
                col=g[i][j]; st=[(i,j)]; comp=[]; seen[i][j]=True
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop(); comp.append((y,x))
                    for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        a,b=y+dy,x+dx
                        if 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and g[a][b]==col and not seen[a][b]:
                            seen[a][b]=True; st.append((a,b))
                res.append((col,comp))
    return res

def f(I,order_key='desc'):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    seq = sorted(comps_of(I),key=lambda t:-t[0]) if order_key=='desc' else sorted(comps_of(I),key=lambda t:t[0])
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            if any(out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            # stop if would become orth-adjacent to different-colored placed cells
            ok=True
            for (yy,xx) in nxt:
                for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy2,xx2=yy+dy,xx+dx
                    if 0<=yy2<H and 0<=xx2<W and out[yy2][xx2]!=c and out[yy2][xx2]!=0:
                        ok=False; break
                if not ok: break
            if not ok: break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    seq=sorted(comps_of(I),key=lambda t:-t[0])      # descending color order
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            if any(out[y][x]!=c and out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out
I=G['Demo pair 1 input']; O=G['Demo pair 1 output']

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    # order: higher color first; within same color, larger component first
    seq=sorted(cs,key=lambda t:(-t[0],-len(t[1])))
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            if any(out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            ok=True
            for (yy,xx) in nxt:
                for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy2,xx2=yy+dy,xx+dx
                    if 0<=yy2<H and 0<=xx2<W and out[yy2][xx2]!=0:
                        ok=False; break
                if not ok: break
            if not ok: break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    seq=sorted(cs,key=lambda t:(t[0],min(x for y,x in t[1])))   # ascending color, tie by leftmost
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            # overlap with placed cells -> stop
            if any(out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            # orth-adjacency to any placed nonzero cell -> stop
            ok=True
            for (yy,xx) in nxt:
                for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy2,xx2=yy+dy,xx+dx
                    if 0<=yy2<H and 0<=xx2<W and out[yy2][xx2]!=0:
                        ok=False; break
                if not ok: break
            if not ok: break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    seq=sorted(cs,key=lambda t:(-len(t[1]),-t[0]))   # size desc, tie color desc
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            if any(out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            ok=True
            for (yy,xx) in nxt:
                for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy2,xx2=yy+dy,xx+dx
                    if 0<=yy2<H and 0<=xx2<W and out[yy2][xx2]!=0:
                        ok=False; break
                if not ok: break
            if not ok: break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    # process by rightmost column descending; tie -> original reading order
    seq=sorted(cs,key=lambda t:(-max(x for y,x in t[1]), min(y for y,x in t[1])))
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c,cp in seq:
        d=0
        while True:
            nxt=[(y,x+d) for y,x in cp]
            if any(x>=W for _,x in nxt) or any(y<0 or y>=H for y,_ in nxt): break
            if any(out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt): break
            ok=True
            for (yy,xx) in nxt:
                for dy,dx in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy2,xx2=yy+dy,xx+dx
                    if 0<=yy2<H and 0<=xx2<W and out[yy2][xx2]!=0:
                        ok=False; break
                if not ok: break
            if not ok: break
            d+=1
            if d>W: break
        for y,x in cp:
            xx=x+d
            if xx<W: out[y][xx]=c
    return out

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    # iteratively slide each component right by 1 while all target cells in bounds & unoccupied (own cells vacated automatically)
    changed=True
    while changed:
        changed=False
        for c,cp in cs:
            tgt=[(y,x+1) for y,x in cp]
            if all(0<=x<W and out[y][x]==0 for y,x in tgt):
                # remove old cells, place shifted
                for y,x in cp: out[y][x]=0
                for y,x in tgt: out[y][x]=c
                changed=True
    return out

import numpy as np
def rule(a):
    a=np.array(a); H,W=a.shape; k=3
    cnts={}
    for x in a.flatten(): cnts[int(x)]=cnts.get(int(x),0)+1
    bg=max(cnts,key=lambda c:cnts[c])
    out=[]
    for i in range(0,H,k):
        row=[]
        for j in range(0,W,k):
            blk=a[i:i+k,j:j+k]
            u,cn=np.unique(blk,return_counts=True)
            others=[(int(u[c]),int(c)) for c in range(len(u)) if u[c]!=bg]
            # rank others by count descending
            rank=sorted(others,key=lambda o:o[1],reverse=True)
            row.append(rank[0][0] if len(others)>=1 else (bg if False else 0))
        out.append(row)
    return out
